verses.text: My brothers and sisters, not many of you should become teachers, because you know teachers will be judged more strictly.
We all stumble in many ways. If someone never slips up in what they say, they’re mature and can control their whole body too.
We put bits in horses’ mouths to make them obey us, and we can guide their whole bodies.
Look at ships too: though they’re large and driven by strong winds, a small rudder steers them wherever the pilot wants.
In the same way, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes big claims. A small spark can set a huge forest on fire.
The tongue is a fire, a whole world of evil among our body parts. It pollutes the whole person, sets the course of life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.
All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures have been tamed by humans,
but no one can tame the tongue. It’s restless and evil, full of deadly poison.
With our tongue we praise our Lord and Father, and with it we curse people made in God’s likeness.
Praise and cursing come from the same mouth. My brothers and sisters, this shouldn’t happen.
Can fresh water and bitter water flow from the same spring?
My brothers and sisters, can a fig tree produce olives, or a grapevine figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.
Who among you is wise and understanding? Let them show it by their good life and deeds done with humility that comes from wisdom.
But if you have bitter envy and selfish ambition in your hearts, don’t brag about it or deny the truth.
That kind of wisdom doesn’t come from above; it’s earthly, unspiritual, and demonic.
Where envy and selfish ambition exist, there’s disorder and every kind of evil practice.
But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peace-loving, considerate, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial and sincere.
Peacemakers who sow peace harvest righteousness.
